“When a woman has a discharge, and the discharge in her body is blood, she is to be in her menstrual impurity seven days, and whoever touches her will be unclean until evening.
Everything on which she lies during her menstrual impurity will be unclean, and everything on which she sits will be unclean.
Whoever touches her bed is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Whoever touches anything on which she sits is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Whether it is the bed or anything on which she sits, when he touches it he will be unclean until evening.
If any man lies with her and her menstrual impurity comes on him, he will be unclean seven days, and every bed on which he lies will be unclean.

“If a woman has a discharge of blood for many days, not at the time of her menstrual impurity, or if she has a discharge beyond the time of her impurity, all the days of the discharge of her uncleanness she is to be as in the days of her impurity. She is unclean.{c}
Every bed on which she lies all the days of her discharge is to be to her like the bed of her impurity, and everything on which she sits will be unclean, like the uncleanness of her impurity.
Whoever touches these things will be unclean and is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
But if she is cleansed of her discharge, she is to count for herself seven days, and after that she will be clean.
On the eighth day she is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest, to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. So the priest is to make atonement for her before Yahweh for the discharge of her uncleanness.
“So you are to keep the Israelites separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness by defiling my tabernacle that is among them.”
This is the law for him who has a discharge, and for him who has an emission of semen so that he becomes unclean by it,
and for her who is unwell with her menstrual impurity, and for anyone who has a discharge, whether male or female, and for the man who lies with a woman who is unclean.

notes.text: Literally “from his flesh,” a euphemism for the genitals. The discharge is probably an abnormal one, such as from gonorrhea or another infection, not a normal emission (verse 16).

The Samaritan Pentateuch, the Septuagint, and a Dead Sea Scroll of Leviticus in paleo-Hebrew script (11QpaleoLev-a) add “all the days of the discharge of his body, whether his body runs with his discharge or is blocked by it.” The Masoretic Text may have lost the words by a scribe’s eye skipping between the similar phrases.
Compare the woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years (Mark 5:25–34).

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they came near before Yahweh and died.{a}

Yahweh said to Moses, “Tell Aaron your brother that he must not come at just any time into the Holy Place inside the veil, in front of the atonement cover{b} that is on the ark, so that he will not die. For I will appear in the cloud above the atonement cover.
This is how Aaron is to come into the Holy Place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

He is to put on the holy linen tunic, and have the linen undergarments on his body, and tie the linen sash around him, and wear the linen turban. These are the holy garments. He is to bathe his body in water and then put them on.
He is to take from the congregation of the Israelites two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
“Aaron is to offer the bull as a sin offering for himself and make atonement for himself and for his house.
Then he is to take the two goats and set them before Yahweh at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Aaron is to cast lots over the two goats, one lot for Yahweh and the other lot for Azazel.{c}
Aaron is to present the goat on which the lot for Yahweh fell and offer it as a sin offering.
But the goat on which the lot for Azazel fell is to be set alive before Yahweh, to make atonement over it,{d} to send it away into the wilderness to Azazel.
“Aaron is to present the bull of the sin offering, which is for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his house. He is to slaughter the bull of the sin offering, which is for himself.
He is to take a censer full of coals of fire from the altar before Yahweh, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and bring it inside the veil.
He is to put the incense on the fire before Yahweh, so that the cloud of the incense covers the atonement cover that is over the testimony,{e} so that he does not die.

He is to take some of the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the atonement cover,{f} and before the atonement cover he is to sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.

“Then he is to slaughter the goat of the sin offering that is for the people and bring its blood inside the veil, and do with its blood as he did with the blood of the bull, sprinkling it on the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover.

So he is to make atonement for the Holy Place, because of the uncleannesses of the Israelites and because of their transgressions, all their sins. He is to do the same for the tent of meeting, which dwells with them in the midst of their uncleannesses.

No one is to be in the tent of meeting from the time he goes in to make atonement in the Holy Place until he comes out and has made atonement for himself, for his house, and for all the assembly of Israel.

Then he is to go out to the altar that is before Yahweh and make atonement for it. He is to take some of the blood of the bull and some of the blood of the goat and put it on the horns of the altar all around.
He is to sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it and consecrate it from the uncleannesses of the Israelites.
“When he has finished making atonement for the Holy Place, the tent of meeting, and the altar, he is to present the live goat.

Aaron is to lay both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities of the Israelites and all their transgressions, all their sins. He is to put them on the head of the goat and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man ready for the task.{g}
The goat will carry on itself all their iniquities to a remote land,{h} and he is to let the goat go free in the wilderness.
“Then Aaron is to come into the tent of meeting and take off the linen garments that he put on when he went into the Holy Place, and leave them there.

He is to bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his garments, and come out and offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.
The fat of the sin offering he is to burn on the altar.
The one who let the goat go to Azazel is to wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after that he may come into the camp.

The bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the Holy Place, are to be carried outside the camp. Their hides, their flesh, and their dung are to be burned with fire.
The one who burns them is to wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after that he may come into the camp.

“This is to be a statute forever for you: in the seventh month (in September–October),{i} on the tenth day of the month, you are to humble yourselves{j} and do no work at all, whether the native-born or the foreigner who resides among you.
For on this day atonement will be made for you, to cleanse you. From all your sins you will be clean before Yahweh.
It is a Sabbath of complete rest{k} for you, and you are to humble yourselves. It is a statute forever.
The priest who is anointed and ordained to serve as priest in his father’s place is to make the atonement. He is to put on the linen garments, the holy garments,

and make atonement for the Most Holy Place,{l} and he is to make atonement for the tent of meeting and for the altar, and he is to make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
This is to be a statute forever for you, to make atonement for the Israelites once a year because of all their sins.” And he did as Yahweh commanded Moses.{m}

notes.text: The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint read “when they offered strange fire before Yahweh and died,” recalling 10:1–2.
Hebrew kapporeth, from the same root as kipper, “to atone.” The traditional “mercy seat” comes from the German of Martin Luther by way of William Tyndale. See the note at Exodus 25:17.

Hebrew la‘aza’zel, “for Azazel,” a word found only in this chapter (verses 8, 10, 26). Its meaning is much debated. (1) A proper name, perhaps of a wilderness demon, matching “for Yahweh” in the same verse; 1 Enoch 8–10 makes Azazel the leader of fallen angels. (2) “The goat that departs,” from ‘ez, “goat,” and ’azal, “go away,” the source of the traditional English “scapegoat” (from Tyndale) and close to the Septuagint’s apopompaios, “the one sent away,” and the Vulgate’s caper emissarius. (3) A place name, “a rugged cliff” or “precipice,” as in some rabbinic tradition. (4) An abstract noun meaning “complete removal.” The name is kept here as it stands in the Hebrew. In no reading is the goat a sacrifice offered to Azazel; it carries Israel’s sins away (verses 21–22).
Or “to make atonement with it,” or “to perform purification on it.” The precise sense of kipper here is debated, since the goat is not slaughtered.
The tablets of the covenant inside the ark (Exodus 25:16, 21).
Literally “on the face of the atonement cover eastward.”
Hebrew ‘itti, a word found only here, perhaps “appointed” or “standing ready.” The Septuagint reads “a man ready at hand.”
Hebrew gezerah, literally “cut off,” a land from which there is no return.

Hebrew “in the seventh month,” counted from the spring new year of Israel’s religious calendar (Exodus 12:2). Because the Hebrew months were lunar, the seventh month (later called Tishri) fell in September–October. This tenth day became Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement (23:26–32).
Literally “afflict your souls,” understood in Jewish tradition as fasting and other self-denial (compare Psalm 35:13; Isaiah 58:3, 5; Acts 27:9, “the Fast”).
Hebrew shabbath shabbathon, a rest of the highest degree.
Literally “the holy sanctuary.”

Hebrew “and he did,” that is, Aaron carried out these instructions when the day came. The Septuagint reads “it shall be done once in the year, as the Lord commanded Moses.” Hebrews 9:6–14, 24–28 interprets this day in light of Christ.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the Israelites and say to them, This is what Yahweh has commanded:
Any man of the house of Israel who slaughters an ox or a lamb or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp,

and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting{a} to offer it as an offering to Yahweh before the tabernacle of Yahweh, bloodguilt will be counted against that man. He has shed blood, and that man will be cut off from among his people.

This is so that the Israelites may bring their sacrifices that they sacrifice in the open field, that they may bring them to Yahweh, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice them as sacrifices of peace offerings to Yahweh.
The priest is to splash the blood against the altar of Yahweh at the entrance of the tent of meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.
So they will no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to the goat demons,{b} after whom they prostitute themselves. This is to be a statute forever for them throughout their generations.
“And you are to say to them, Any man of the house of Israel, or of the foreigners who reside among them, who offers a burnt offering or sacrifice
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to Yahweh, that man will be cut off from his people.
“If any man of the house of Israel or of the foreigners who reside among them eats any blood, I will set my face against that person who eats blood and will cut him off from among his people.
For the life{c} of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives, for it is the blood that makes atonement by means of the life.{d}
Therefore I have said to the Israelites, No person among you may eat blood, nor may any foreigner who resides among you eat blood.
Any man of the Israelites, or of the foreigners who reside among them, who hunts and catches a wild animal or a bird that may be eaten is to pour out its blood and cover it with dust.

For the life of all flesh is its blood; it is its life.{e} Therefore I have said to the Israelites, You must not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood. Whoever eats it will be cut off.

Every person who eats what dies by itself or what is torn by beasts, whether he is native-born or a foreigner, is to wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening; then he will be clean.
But if he does not wash them or bathe his body, he will bear his iniquity.”

notes.text: The Septuagint, the Samaritan Pentateuch, and a Dead Sea Scroll of Leviticus (4QLev-d) add here “to make it a burnt offering or a peace offering to Yahweh, to be accepted as a pleasing aroma, and slaughters it outside, and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting.” Another scroll, 11QpaleoLev-a, has the shorter text of the Masoretic Text, which is followed here.

Hebrew se‘irim, literally “hairy ones” or “goats,” here goat-like demons or idols thought to live in the wilderness (Isaiah 13:21; 34:14; 2 Chronicles 11:15). The Septuagint reads “vain things” (idols).
Hebrew nephesh, “soul,” “life,” or “person”; so throughout verses 11–14.
Or “makes atonement for the life” or “as a life” (in place of the life). The Hebrew bannephesh can be read “by means of the life” or “in exchange for the life.” Compare Hebrews 9:22.
The Hebrew of this phrase is difficult, literally “its blood is in its life.”

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, I am Yahweh your God.
You must not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived, and you must not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. You must not walk in their statutes.
You are to do my judgments and keep my statutes, walking in them. I am Yahweh your God.
You are to keep my statutes and my judgments; the person who does them will live by them.{a} I am Yahweh.
“None of you is to approach any close relative{b} to uncover nakedness.{c} I am Yahweh.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father, that is, the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother; you must not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife; it is your father’s nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether born at home or born outside.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, for their nakedness is your own nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter, born to your father; she is your sister.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister; she is your father’s close relative.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister, for she is your mother’s close relative.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your father’s brother; you must not approach his wife. She is your aunt.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law. She is your son’s wife; you must not uncover her nakedness.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife; it is your brother’s nakedness.{d}
You must not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You must not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter to uncover her nakedness. They are close relatives; it is depravity.{e}
You must not take a woman as a rival wife to her sister, to uncover her nakedness while her sister is still alive.{f}
“You must not approach a woman to uncover her nakedness while she is unclean in her menstrual impurity.
You must not lie carnally with your neighbor’s wife, to become unclean with her.
You must not give any of your offspring to make them pass through{g} to Molech,{h} and so profane the name of your God. I am Yahweh.
You must not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is an abomination.{i}
You must not lie with any animal to become unclean with it, and a woman must not stand before an animal to mate with it; it is a perversion.{j}
“Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these things, for by all these the nations I am driving out before you have made themselves unclean.
The land became unclean, so I punished its iniquity upon it, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
But you are to keep my statutes and my judgments and not do any of these abominations, neither the native-born nor the foreigner who resides among you
(for the people of the land who were before you did all these abominations, and the land became unclean),{k}
so that the land does not vomit you out when you make it unclean, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
For whoever does any of these abominations, the persons who do them will be cut off from among their people.
So keep my charge, not doing any of the abominable customs that were done before you, and do not make yourselves unclean by them. I am Yahweh your God.”

notes.text: Quoted in Nehemiah 9:29; Ezekiel 20:11; Romans 10:5; Galatians 3:12.
Literally “flesh of his flesh.”
“Uncover nakedness” is a Hebrew idiom for sexual relations; so throughout this chapter.
Compare the duty of levirate marriage in Deuteronomy 25:5–10, which applies when the brother has died without a son.
Hebrew zimmah, a deliberate, shameful wickedness.
The Hebrew can also be read as banning taking a second wife in general (“a woman in addition to another”), as the Damascus Document of Qumran understood it, but the usual sense is a sister.
Hebrew leha‘abir, “to make pass over,” often understood as passing children through fire (2 Kings 23:10) as child sacrifice. The Septuagint reads “to serve a ruler.”

Hebrew molek, probably a deity to whom children were sacrificed, though some scholars take it as the name of a kind of sacrifice. The vowels may be those of bosheth, “shame,” added to the consonants of melek, “king.” The Septuagint here reads archon, “ruler,” and elsewhere (20:2) Moloch.
Hebrew to‘evah, something detestable or abhorrent; so in verses 26–30.
Hebrew tevel, “confusion,” a mixing of what should be kept apart.
A Dead Sea Scroll of Leviticus (11QpaleoLev-a) sets this verse off with marks resembling parentheses, as this translation also does.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to all the congregation of the Israelites and say to them, You are to be holy, for I, Yahweh your God, am holy.{a}
Each of you is to revere his mother and his father, and you are to keep my Sabbaths. I am Yahweh your God.
Do not turn to worthless idols{b} or make for yourselves gods of cast metal. I am Yahweh your God.
“When you sacrifice a sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh, sacrifice it so that you are accepted.
It is to be eaten on the day you sacrifice it or on the next day. Whatever is left over until the third day is to be burned with fire.
If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is a foul thing;{c} it will not be accepted.
Whoever eats it will bear his iniquity, because he has profaned what is holy to Yahweh, and that person will be cut off from his people.
“When you reap the harvest of your land, you must not reap to the very edge of your field, and you must not gather the gleanings of your harvest.
You must not strip your vineyard bare or gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard. You are to leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am Yahweh your God.
“You must not steal, you must not deceive, and you must not lie to one another.
You must not swear by my name falsely and so profane the name of your God. I am Yahweh.
“You must not oppress your neighbor or rob him. The wages of a hired worker must not remain with you all night until morning.
You must not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block in front of the blind, but you are to fear your God. I am Yahweh.
“You must not do injustice in judgment. You must not show partiality to the poor or defer to the great. In righteousness you are to judge your neighbor.
You must not go around as a slanderer among your people. You must not stand against the blood{d} of your neighbor. I am Yahweh.
“You must not hate your brother in your heart. You are to reprove your neighbor plainly, so that you do not bear sin because of him.{e}
You must not take vengeance or bear a grudge against the children of your people, but you are to love your neighbor as yourself.{f} I am Yahweh.
“You are to keep my statutes. You must not let your livestock breed with another kind. You must not sow your field with two kinds of seed, nor put on a garment made of two kinds of material.{g}

“If a man lies carnally with a woman who is a slave, assigned to another man{h} but not at all ransomed or given her freedom, there is to be an inquiry.{i} They are not to be put to death, because she was not free.
He is to bring his guilt offering to Yahweh, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, a ram as a guilt offering.
The priest is to make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before Yahweh for his sin that he has committed, and he will be forgiven for the sin that he has committed.
“When you come into the land and plant any kind of tree for food, you are to regard its fruit as forbidden.{j} For three years it will be forbidden to you; it must not be eaten.
In the fourth year all its fruit is to be holy, an offering of praise to Yahweh.
But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that it may increase its yield for you. I am Yahweh your God.
“You must not eat anything with the blood.{k} You must not practice divination or soothsaying.{l}
You must not cut off the hair at the sides of your head or mar the edges of your beard.
You must not make any cuts in your flesh for the dead or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am Yahweh.
“Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, so that the land does not fall into prostitution and the land become full of depravity.
You are to keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am Yahweh.
“Do not turn to mediums or to spiritists;{m} do not seek them out to be made unclean by them. I am Yahweh your God.
“You are to rise up before the gray head and honor the face of an old man, and you are to fear your God. I am Yahweh.
“When a foreigner resides with you in your land, you must not mistreat him.
The foreigner who resides with you is to be to you like the native-born among you, and you are to love him as yourself, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.
“You must not do injustice in judgment, in measurement of length, weight, or quantity.
You are to have honest scales, honest weights, an honest dry measure, and an honest liquid measure.{n} I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
You are to keep all my statutes and all my judgments and do them. I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: Quoted in 1 Peter 1:16.
Hebrew ’elilim, “nothings” or “worthless things,” a scornful word for idols that sounds like ’elohim, “gods.”
Hebrew piggul, meat that has become ritually offensive; see the note at 7:18.
That is, do nothing that endangers your neighbor’s life, whether by false testimony or by standing idle. The Hebrew is difficult.
Or “so that you do not incur sin on his account” (by letting him go on in it).
Quoted by Jesus as the second great commandment (Matthew 22:39; Mark 12:31; Luke 10:27), and in Romans 13:9; Galatians 5:14; James 2:8.
Hebrew sha‘atnez, a word of uncertain, perhaps foreign, origin; Deuteronomy 22:11 explains it as wool and linen together.
Or “betrothed to another man.” The Hebrew neḥerepheth occurs only here.
Hebrew biqqoreth, found only here; perhaps “an inquiry,” “compensation,” or “punishment.” The Septuagint reads “they shall be visited with punishment.”
Literally “you are to regard its foreskin as its foreskin,” that is, as uncircumcised; so later in the verse.
Or “over the blood,” perhaps a rite at the place of slaughter. The Septuagint reads “on the mountains.”
Two kinds of forbidden divination; the exact practices are uncertain.
Hebrew ’oboth and yidde‘onim, those who consult the spirits of the dead and those who claim special knowledge. The exact meanings are uncertain.

Hebrew “an honest ephah and an honest hin.” The ephah was a dry measure of about 3/5 bushel (about 22 liters), and the hin a liquid measure of about 1 gallon (about 3.7 liters). Both stand here for all measures of volume.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

“Say to the Israelites, Any man of the Israelites, or of the foreigners who reside in Israel, who gives any of his offspring to Molech{a} is surely to be put to death. The people of the land are to stone him with stones.
I myself will set my face against that man and cut him off from among his people, because he has given some of his offspring to Molech, to make my sanctuary unclean and to profane my holy name.
And if the people of the land ever close their eyes to that man when he gives any of his offspring to Molech, and do not put him to death,
then I myself will set my face against that man and against his clan, and will cut off from among their people him and all who follow him in prostituting themselves after Molech.
“The person who turns to mediums and spiritists, to prostitute himself after them, I will set my face against that person and cut him off from among his people.
Consecrate yourselves, then, and be holy, for I am Yahweh your God.
Keep my statutes and do them. I am Yahweh who makes you holy.
“Anyone who curses his father or his mother is surely to be put to death. He has cursed his father or his mother; his blood is on him.{b}
“If a man commits adultery with the wife of a man, if he commits adultery with the wife of his neighbor,{c} both the adulterer and the adulteress are surely to be put to death.
If a man lies with his father’s wife, he has uncovered his father’s nakedness. Both of them are surely to be put to death; their blood is on them.
If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them are surely to be put to death. They have committed a perversion; their blood is on them.
If a man lies with a male as one lies with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination. They are surely to be put to death; their blood is on them.
If a man takes a woman and her mother, it is depravity. He and they are to be burned with fire, so that there is no depravity among you.
If a man lies with an animal, he is surely to be put to death, and you are to kill the animal.
If a woman approaches any animal to mate with it, you are to kill the woman and the animal. They are surely to be put to death; their blood is on them.

“If a man takes his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace,{d} and they are to be cut off in the sight of the children of their people. He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness; he will bear his iniquity.

If a man lies with a woman during her menstrual period and uncovers her nakedness, he has laid bare her flow, and she has uncovered the flow of her blood. Both of them are to be cut off from among their people.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister or of your father’s sister, for that is to lay bare one’s close relative. They will bear their iniquity.
If a man lies with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness. They will bear their sin; they will die childless.
If a man takes his brother’s wife, it is impurity.{e} He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness; they will be childless.
“You are to keep all my statutes and all my judgments and do them, so that the land where I am bringing you to live does not vomit you out.
You must not walk in the statutes of the nation that I am driving out before you, for they did all these things, and I loathed them.
But I have said to you, You will possess their land, and I will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am Yahweh your God, who has set you apart from the peoples.

You are therefore to distinguish between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean bird and the clean. You must not make yourselves detestable by animal or by bird or by anything that creeps on the ground, which I have set apart for you as unclean.
You are to be holy to me, for I, Yahweh, am holy, and I have set you apart from the peoples to be mine.
“A man or a woman who is a medium or a spiritist{f} is surely to be put to death. They are to stone them with stones; their blood is on them.”

notes.text: See the note at 18:21. Here the Septuagint reads Moloch.
That is, he is responsible for his own death; so throughout this chapter.

The repeated clause is often taken as an accidental duplication in copying. The Septuagint reads “Whoever commits adultery with the wife of a man, or whoever commits adultery with the wife of his neighbor.”
Hebrew ḥesed, usually “steadfast love,” here in a rare negative sense, “shame.”
Hebrew niddah, the word used for menstrual impurity.
Literally “in whom there is a medium (’ov) or a spirit of knowing.” See the note at 19:31.

verses.text: Yahweh said to Moses, “Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them, No one is to make himself unclean for a dead person among his people,
except for his close relatives:{a} his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
and his virgin sister who is near to him because she has had no husband; for her he may make himself unclean.
He must not make himself unclean as a husband among his people, and so profane himself.{b}
They must not make bald spots on their heads, or shave off the edges of their beards, or make any cuts in their flesh.
They are to be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God, for they offer the offerings by fire to Yahweh, the food{c} of their God; so they are to be holy.
They must not marry a woman who is a prostitute or who has been defiled,{d} nor marry a woman divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
You are to treat him as holy, for he offers the food of your God. He is to be holy to you, for I, Yahweh, who makes you holy, am holy.
If the daughter of any priest profanes herself by prostitution, she profanes her father; she is to be burned with fire.

“The priest who is greatest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been ordained to wear the garments, must not let the hair of his head hang loose or tear his clothes.
He must not go in to any dead body or make himself unclean even for his father or his mother.
He must not go out of the sanctuary or profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am Yahweh.
He is to take a wife in her virginity.
A widow, a divorced woman, or one who has been defiled as a prostitute, these he must not marry. He is to take as his wife a virgin from his own people,
so that he does not profane his offspring among his people, for I am Yahweh who makes him holy.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron and say, None of your offspring throughout their generations who has a defect may approach to offer the food of his God.
For no man who has a defect may approach: a man who is blind or lame, or who has a disfigured face{e} or a limb too long,
or a man who has a broken foot or a broken hand,
or is a hunchback or a dwarf,{f} or has a spot in his eye, or eczema or scabs, or crushed testicles.
No man of the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a defect may come near to offer the offerings by fire to Yahweh. He has a defect; he must not come near to offer the food of his God.
He may eat the food of his God, both of the most holy and of the holy things,
but he must not go in to the veil or approach the altar, because he has a defect, so that he does not profane my holy places,{g} for I am Yahweh who makes them holy.”
So Moses spoke to Aaron and to his sons and to all the Israelites.

notes.text: Literally “his flesh who is near to him.”

The Hebrew is difficult, literally “a husband (or master) must not make himself unclean among his people.” It may mean that a priest must not defile himself for the relatives of his wife, or that as a leader among his people he must not defile himself. The Septuagint reads “He shall not defile himself suddenly among his people.”
Literally “bread”; so throughout this chapter and the next.
Or “a woman who has been violated.” The Hebrew ḥalalah means “profaned.”
Hebrew ḥarum, perhaps “with a split nose” or a similar facial deformity; the meaning is uncertain.
Or “emaciated.” The meanings of several terms in this verse are uncertain.
Or “my sanctuaries.” The Septuagint reads “the sanctuary of his God.”

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron and to his sons, so that they keep themselves apart{a} from the holy things of the Israelites, which they consecrate to me, and do not profane my holy name. I am Yahweh.

Say to them, If any man among all your offspring throughout your generations approaches the holy things that the Israelites consecrate to Yahweh while he has his uncleanness on him, that person will be cut off from my presence. I am Yahweh.

No man of the offspring of Aaron who has a defiling skin disease{b} or a discharge may eat of the holy things until he is clean. Whoever touches anything made unclean by a dead person, or a man who has an emission of semen,
or a man who touches any swarming thing by which he is made unclean, or a person by whom he is made unclean, whatever his uncleanness may be,
the person who touches any such thing will be unclean until evening and must not eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water.
When the sun goes down he will be clean, and afterward he may eat of the holy things, for it is his food.
He must not eat what dies by itself or what is torn by beasts, becoming unclean by it. I am Yahweh.
They are to keep my charge, so that they do not bear sin for it and die by it when they profane it. I am Yahweh who makes them holy.
“No outsider{c} may eat a holy thing. A priest’s guest or a hired worker may not eat a holy thing.
But if a priest buys a person with his money, that one may eat of it, and those born in his house may eat of his food.
If a priest’s daughter is married to an outsider, she may not eat of the contribution of the holy things.
But if a priest’s daughter is widowed or divorced and has no child and returns to her father’s house as in her youth, she may eat of her father’s food. But no outsider may eat of it.
If a man eats a holy thing unintentionally, he is to add a fifth of its value to it and give the holy thing to the priest.
The priests must not profane the holy things of the Israelites that they contribute to Yahweh,
and so cause them to bear iniquity requiring a guilt offering{d} when they eat their holy things, for I am Yahweh who makes them holy.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

“Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the Israelites and say to them, Any man of the house of Israel, or of the foreigners in Israel, who presents his offering, whether for any of their vows or any of their freewill offerings that they present to Yahweh as a burnt offering,
to be accepted for you it must be a male without defect, from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
You must not present anything that has a defect, for it will not be accepted for you.

When anyone presents a sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh to fulfill a vow{e} or as a freewill offering, from the herd or the flock, it must be without defect to be accepted; there must be no defect in it.
Anything blind or injured or maimed, or having a running sore or eczema or scabs, you must not present to Yahweh or give any of them as an offering by fire on the altar to Yahweh.
You may present an ox or a lamb that has a limb too long or too short{f} as a freewill offering, but it will not be accepted for a vow.
Anything with its testicles bruised, crushed, torn, or cut you must not present to Yahweh; you must not do this in your land.
Nor may you present any of these as the food of your God from the hand of a foreigner. Because their corruption is in them, there is a defect in them; they will not be accepted for you.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“When an ox or a sheep or a goat is born, it is to remain seven days with its mother, and from the eighth day on it will be accepted as an offering by fire to Yahweh.
But whether it is an ox or a sheep, you must not slaughter it and its young on the same day.
When you sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving to Yahweh, sacrifice it so that you are accepted.
It is to be eaten on the same day; you must not leave any of it until morning. I am Yahweh.
“So you are to keep my commandments and do them. I am Yahweh.
You must not profane my holy name, so that I may be treated as holy among the Israelites. I am Yahweh who makes you holy,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: Or “deal carefully with.” The Hebrew nazar is related to nazir, “Nazirite,” one set apart.
Hebrew tsara‘at; see the note at 13:2. The Septuagint reads lepra; the condition is not modern leprosy (Hansen’s disease).
Hebrew zar, “stranger,” here anyone who is not of a priestly family.
Hebrew ‘awon ’ashmah, “iniquity of guilt”; see the note on ’asham at 5:6.
Or “a special vow.” The Hebrew lephalle’ means “to set apart” or “to make extraordinary.”
Hebrew sarua‘ weqalut, probably “deformed or stunted.” The Septuagint reads “with the ears cut off, or that has lost its tail.”

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, The appointed feasts{a} of Yahweh that you are to proclaim as holy convocations, these are my appointed feasts.
“Six days work may be done, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a holy convocation. You must not do any work; it is a Sabbath to Yahweh in all your dwellings.
“These are the appointed feasts of Yahweh, the holy convocations that you are to proclaim at their appointed times.
In the first month (in March–April),{b} on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight,{c} is Yahweh’s Passover.{d}
On the fifteenth day of the same month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread to Yahweh. For seven days you are to eat unleavened bread.
On the first day you are to have a holy convocation; you must not do any ordinary work.{e}
For seven days you are to present an offering by fire to Yahweh. On the seventh day is a holy convocation; you must not do any ordinary work.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, When you come into the land that I am giving you and reap its harvest, you are to bring the sheaf{f} of the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest.
He is to wave the sheaf before Yahweh so that you may be accepted. On the day after the Sabbath{g} the priest is to wave it.
On the day you wave the sheaf, you are to offer a male lamb a year old without defect as a burnt offering to Yahweh,
and its grain offering, about 4 quarts{h} of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering by fire to Yahweh, a pleasing aroma, and its drink offering of wine, about 1 quart.{i}
You must not eat bread or roasted grain or fresh grain until this very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. It is a statute forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
“You are to count for yourselves from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you brought the sheaf of the wave offering, seven full Sabbaths.{j}
You are to count fifty days to the day after the seventh Sabbath.{k} Then you are to present a new grain offering to Yahweh.
From your dwellings you are to bring two loaves of bread for a wave offering, made of about 4 quarts{l} of fine flour. They are to be baked with leaven, as firstfruits to Yahweh.

With the bread you are to present seven male lambs a year old without defect, one young bull, and two rams. They are to be a burnt offering to Yahweh, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.
You are to offer one male goat as a sin offering and two male lambs a year old as a sacrifice of peace offerings.
The priest is to wave them with the bread of the firstfruits as a wave offering before Yahweh, with the two lambs. They are to be holy to Yahweh for the priest.
On this same day you are to make a proclamation; it is to be a holy convocation for you. You must not do any ordinary work. It is a statute forever in all your dwellings throughout your generations.

“When you reap the harvest of your land, you must not reap to the very edge of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest. You are to leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am Yahweh your God.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

“Speak to the Israelites, saying, In the seventh month (in September–October),{m} on the first day of the month, you are to have a complete rest, a memorial proclaimed with a blast of horns,{n} a holy convocation.
You must not do any ordinary work, and you are to present an offering by fire to Yahweh.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

“But on the tenth day of this seventh month (in September–October){o} is the Day of Atonement.{p} It is to be a holy convocation for you. You are to humble yourselves{q} and present an offering by fire to Yahweh.
You must not do any work on this very day, for it is a day of atonement, to make atonement for you before Yahweh your God.
For any person who does not humble himself on this very day will be cut off from his people.
And any person who does any work on this very day, I will destroy that person from among his people.
You must not do any work. It is a statute forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
It is to be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you are to humble yourselves. On the ninth day of the month at evening,{r} from evening to evening, you are to keep your Sabbath.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites, saying, On the fifteenth day of this seventh month (in September–October){s} is the Feast of Booths{t} for seven days to Yahweh.
On the first day is a holy convocation; you must not do any ordinary work.

For seven days you are to present an offering by fire to Yahweh. On the eighth day you are to have a holy convocation and present an offering by fire to Yahweh. It is a solemn assembly;{u} you must not do any ordinary work.

“These are the appointed feasts of Yahweh that you are to proclaim as holy convocations, for presenting offerings by fire to Yahweh: burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, each on its own day,
besides the Sabbaths of Yahweh, and besides your gifts, besides all your vows, and besides all your freewill offerings that you give to Yahweh.

“But on the fifteenth day of the seventh month (in September–October),{v} when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you are to celebrate the feast of Yahweh for seven days. On the first day is a complete rest, and on the eighth day is a complete rest.

On the first day you are to take for yourselves the fruit of majestic trees,{w} branches of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook, and you are to rejoice before Yahweh your God for seven days.
You are to celebrate it as a feast to Yahweh for seven days in the year. It is a statute forever throughout your generations; you are to celebrate it in the seventh month.
You are to live in booths for seven days. Every native-born Israelite is to live in booths,
so that your generations may know that I made the Israelites live in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.”
So Moses declared the appointed feasts of Yahweh to the Israelites.

notes.text: Hebrew mo‘adim, “appointed times,” the fixed festivals of the year.

Hebrew “in the first month.” The months are counted from the spring new year of Israel’s religious calendar (Exodus 12:2). This month was called Abib (“ripe grain,” Exodus 13:4) and later Nisan (Esther 3:7). Because the Hebrew months were lunar, with an extra month added in some years, the first month did not match a modern month exactly but fell in March–April.
Hebrew ben ha‘arbayim, literally “between the two evenings,” the time between sunset and full dark (or, in later practice, between midafternoon and sunset). See the note at Exodus 12:6.
Hebrew pesaḥ, from pasaḥ, “to pass over” (Exodus 12:13, 23, 27).
Literally “work of labor,” that is, one’s regular occupational work, as distinct from preparing food (compare Exodus 12:16).
Hebrew ‘omer, a sheaf of grain, here the first sheaf of the barley harvest. Elsewhere the same word is a dry measure (Exodus 16:36).

Which Sabbath is meant was debated in ancient Judaism. The Pharisees and later rabbis took it as the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread (the Septuagint here reads “the day after the first day”), while the Sadducees and others took it as the weekly Sabbath during the feast, so that the count always began on a Sunday.
Hebrew “two tenths,” that is, two tenths of an ephah, about 4.4 liters.
Hebrew “a fourth of a hin,” about 0.9 liter.
Or “seven full weeks.”
This day, the Feast of Weeks (Exodus 34:22; Deuteronomy 16:10), is called in Greek Pentecost, “fiftieth” (Acts 2:1).
Hebrew “two tenths,” that is, two tenths of an ephah, about 4.4 liters.

Hebrew “in the seventh month,” counted from the spring new year; later called Tishri (1 Kings 8:2 calls it Ethanim). Because the Hebrew months were lunar, it fell in September–October. In later Judaism this first day became Rosh Hashanah, the civil New Year.
Hebrew teru‘ah, a shout or blast, usually understood as the sounding of the shofar (ram’s horn). The Septuagint reads “a memorial of trumpets.”
Hebrew “the tenth day of this seventh month” (Tishri); see the note at verse 24.
Hebrew yom hakkippurim, “day of atonements,” Yom Kippur. See chapter 16.
Literally “afflict your souls”; see the note at 16:29. So in verses 29 and 32.
Since the Hebrew day began at sunset, the observance runs from the evening that ends the ninth day to the evening of the tenth.
Hebrew “the fifteenth day of this seventh month” (Tishri); see the note at verse 24.
Hebrew sukkoth, “booths” or “huts,” temporary shelters of branches. Traditionally the Feast of Tabernacles.
Hebrew ‘atsereth, perhaps “closing assembly.” The Septuagint reads “a time of release.”
Hebrew “the fifteenth day of the seventh month” (Tishri); see the note at verse 24.
Hebrew ‘ets hadar, “splendid trees,” identified in Jewish tradition as the citron (etrog).

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of beaten olives for the light, to keep a lamp burning{a} continually.
Outside the veil of the testimony in the tent of meeting, Aaron is to arrange it from evening to morning before Yahweh continually. It is a statute forever throughout your generations.
He is to arrange the lamps on the lampstand of pure gold{b} before Yahweh continually.
“You are to take fine flour and bake twelve loaves{c} from it; each loaf is to be made of about 4 quarts.{d}
You are to set them in two rows, six to a row,{e} on the table of pure gold before Yahweh.
You are to put pure frankincense on each row, so that it may be a memorial portion{f} for the bread, an offering by fire to Yahweh.
Every Sabbath day he is to arrange it before Yahweh continually. It is from the Israelites as a covenant forever.
It is to belong to Aaron and his sons, and they are to eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy for him from the offerings by fire to Yahweh, a perpetual due.”
Now the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the Israelites, and the son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name{g} and cursed. So they brought him to Moses. His mother’s name was Shelomith,{h} the daughter of Dibri,{i} of the tribe of Dan.{j}
They put him in custody until the will of Yahweh should be made clear to them.
Then Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Bring the one who cursed outside the camp, and let all who heard him lay their hands on his head, and let all the congregation stone him.
And speak to the Israelites, saying, Anyone who curses his God will bear his sin.
Whoever blasphemes the name of Yahweh is surely to be put to death. All the congregation is to stone him. The foreigner as well as the native-born, when he blasphemes the Name, is to be put to death.
“Whoever strikes down any human life is surely to be put to death.
Whoever strikes down the life of an animal is to make it good, life for life.
When a man causes a disfigurement in his neighbor, as he has done, so is it to be done to him:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth.{k} As he has caused a disfigurement in a person, so is it to be done to him.
Whoever kills an animal is to make it good, and whoever kills a person is to be put to death.
You are to have one standard of judgment for the foreigner and for the native-born, for I am Yahweh your God.”
So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they brought the one who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones. The Israelites did as Yahweh commanded Moses.

notes.text: Literally “to cause a lamp to go up.”
Literally “the pure lampstand,” that is, the lampstand of pure gold (Exodus 25:31).
Or “twelve rings of bread,” the bread of the Presence (Exodus 25:30).
Hebrew “two tenths,” that is, two tenths of an ephah, about 4.4 liters.
Or “in two piles, six to a pile.”
Hebrew ’azkarah; see the note at 2:2.

Hebrew hashshem, “the Name,” that is, the name Yahweh (verse 16). From this passage comes the Jewish practice of saying HaShem, “the Name,” in place of the divine name. The Septuagint reads “named the Name.”
Shelomith means “peaceful,” from shalom, “peace.” The Septuagint spells it Salomith.
Dibri perhaps means “talkative” or “my word.” The Septuagint spells it Dabri.
Dan means “judge” (Genesis 30:6).
This principle of equivalent justice (lex talionis) set a limit on punishment and was applied by judges, not by private revenge. Compare Exodus 21:23–25; Deuteronomy 19:21; Matthew 5:38–39.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, When you come into the land that I am giving you, the land is to keep a Sabbath to Yahweh.
For six years you are to sow your field, and for six years you are to prune your vineyard and gather in its produce.
But in the seventh year there is to be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land, a Sabbath to Yahweh. You must not sow your field or prune your vineyard.
You must not reap what grows of itself from your harvest or gather the grapes of your untended vine.{a} It is to be a year of complete rest for the land.
The Sabbath produce of the land will be food for you: for yourself, for your male and female slaves, for your hired worker, and for the resident alien who lives with you,
and for your livestock and for the wild animals in your land. All its produce is to be for food.
“You are to count seven Sabbaths of years, seven times seven years, so that the time of the seven Sabbaths of years amounts to forty-nine years.
Then on the tenth day of the seventh month (in September–October){b} you are to sound the loud horn.{c} On the Day of Atonement you are to sound the horn throughout all your land.

You are to consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty{d} throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It is to be a jubilee{e} for you; each of you is to return to his property, and each of you is to return to his clan.
That fiftieth year is to be a jubilee for you. You must not sow, or reap what grows of itself, or gather the grapes of its untended vines.
For it is a jubilee; it is to be holy to you. You may eat its produce directly from the field.
In this year of jubilee each of you is to return to his property.
If you sell anything to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor, you must not wrong one another.
You are to buy from your neighbor according to the number of years after the jubilee, and he is to sell to you according to the number of years of crops.
If the years are many, you are to increase the price, and if the years are few, you are to reduce the price, for it is the number of crops that he is selling to you.
You must not wrong one another, but you are to fear your God, for I am Yahweh your God.
“So you are to do my statutes and keep my judgments and do them, and you will live in the land securely.
The land will yield its fruit, and you will eat your fill and live in it securely.
If you say, ‘What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather in our produce?’
I will command my blessing for you in the sixth year, so that it will yield produce for three years.
When you sow in the eighth year, you will eat from the old produce; until the ninth year, when its produce comes in, you will eat the old.
“The land must not be sold permanently,{f} for the land is mine. You are foreigners and residents with me.
Throughout the land of your possession you are to allow redemption of the land.
“If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his property, his nearest redeemer{g} is to come and redeem what his brother has sold.
If a man has no one to redeem it, but he himself prospers and finds enough to redeem it,
he is to count the years since its sale, refund the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his property.
But if he does not find enough to repay him, what he sold will remain in the hand of the buyer until the year of jubilee. In the jubilee it is to be released, and he will return to his property.
“If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, its redemption right will last until a full year after its sale; for a full year{h} he may redeem it.
If it is not redeemed within a full year, the house in the walled city will belong permanently to the buyer throughout his generations. It will not be released in the jubilee.
But houses in villages that have no wall around them are to be counted as part of the fields of the land. They may be redeemed, and they are to be released in the jubilee.
As for the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities they possess, the Levites are to have a permanent right of redemption.

And if one of the Levites redeems,{i} then the house that was sold in a city of their possession is to be released in the jubilee, for the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the Israelites.
But the pastureland around their cities may not be sold, for that is their permanent possession.
“If your brother becomes poor and cannot support himself{j} among you, you are to support him; he is to live with you as a foreigner and resident.
Do not take interest or profit{k} from him, but fear your God, so that your brother may live with you.
You must not lend him your money at interest or give him your food for profit.
I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, to be your God.
“If your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you must not make him serve as a slave.
He is to be with you as a hired worker or a resident. He is to serve with you until the year of jubilee.
Then he and his children with him are to go out from you and return to his own clan, and he is to return to the property of his fathers.
For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; they must not be sold as slaves are sold.
You must not rule over him harshly, but you are to fear your God.
As for your male and female slaves whom you may have, you may buy male and female slaves from the nations around you.
You may also buy them from the children of the foreigners who reside among you and from their clans that are with you, who have been born in your land, and they may become your property.

You may leave them as an inheritance to your children after you, to possess as property. You may make them serve permanently. But over your brothers the Israelites you must not rule harshly, one over another.
“If a foreigner or resident with you prospers, and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to the foreigner or resident with you or to a member of the foreigner’s clan,
after he has sold himself he is to have the right of redemption. One of his brothers may redeem him,
or his uncle or his uncle’s son may redeem him, or any close relative from his clan may redeem him. Or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.

He is to count with his buyer from the year he sold himself to him until the year of jubilee, and the price of his sale is to be in proportion to the number of years. His time with him is to be reckoned as that of a hired worker.
If there are still many years left, he is to pay back for his redemption a share of the price for which he was bought, in proportion to them.
If only a few years remain until the year of jubilee, he is to count with him and pay back for his redemption in proportion to his years.
He is to be with him as a worker hired year by year; he must not rule over him harshly in your sight.
If he is not redeemed by these means, he is to go out in the year of jubilee, he and his children with him.
For the Israelites are servants to me. They are my servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.”

notes.text: Hebrew nazir, literally “your Nazirite,” that is, a vine left unpruned, like the uncut hair of a Nazirite (Numbers 6:5).

Hebrew “in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month,” counted from the spring new year of the religious calendar; the month later called Tishri, which, being lunar, fell in September–October. See the notes at 16:29 and 23:24.
Hebrew shophar teru‘ah, “a horn of blasting,” the ram’s horn.
Hebrew deror, a legal term for release from debt and servitude. Quoted on the Liberty Bell in Philadelphia; compare Isaiah 61:1; Luke 4:18–19.

Hebrew yovel, “ram” or “ram’s horn,” from the horn blown to announce the year. The Latin jubilaeus, from which “jubilee” comes, was influenced by jubilare, “to shout for joy.” The Septuagint reads “a year of release.”
Hebrew litsmithuth, “for complete cutting off,” that is, beyond the right of redemption.
Hebrew go’el, the nearest kinsman, responsible to redeem property and persons and to avenge blood (Ruth 3:12–13; Numbers 35:19).
Literally “days.”
The Hebrew is difficult. The Latin Vulgate reads “If it is not redeemed,” which suits the context, and many interpreters supply a negative.
Literally “his hand falters.”
Hebrew neshekh and tarbith, probably interest taken in advance (literally “bite”) and interest added at repayment.

verses.text: “You must not make idols{a} for yourselves, or set up a carved image or a sacred pillar for yourselves, and you must not place a carved stone{b} in your land to bow down to it, for I am Yahweh your God.
You are to keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am Yahweh.{c}
“If you walk in my statutes and keep my commandments and do them,
I will give you your rains in their season, the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will yield their fruit.
Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will last until sowing time. You will eat your bread to the full and live securely in your land.
I will give peace in the land, and you will lie down with no one to make you afraid. I will remove harmful beasts from the land, and the sword will not pass through your land.
You will chase your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand, and your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
I will turn to you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will confirm my covenant with you.
You will eat old stored grain, and you will clear out the old to make room for the new.
I will set my dwelling{d} among you, and my soul will not reject you.
I will walk among you and will be your God, and you will be my people.{e}
I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, so that you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.
“But if you do not listen to me and do not do all these commandments,
if you reject my statutes, and if your soul rejects my judgments, so that you do not do all my commandments but break my covenant,
then I will do this to you: I will appoint terror over you, wasting disease and fever that consume the eyes and make the soul waste away. You will sow your seed in vain, for your enemies will eat it.
I will set my face against you, and you will be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one is pursuing you.
And if in spite of this you do not listen to me, then I will discipline you seven times more for your sins.
I will break the pride of your power. I will make your sky like iron and your land like bronze.
Your strength will be spent in vain, for your land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not yield their fruit.
“If you walk contrary{f} to me and are not willing to listen to me, I will strike you seven times more, according to your sins.
I will let loose among you the wild animals, which will bereave you of your children, destroy your livestock, and make you few, so that your roads become deserted.
“If by these things you are not corrected toward me, but walk contrary to me,
then I myself will also walk contrary to you, and I myself will strike you seven times for your sins.
I will bring a sword upon you that will execute the vengeance of the covenant. When you gather in your cities, I will send pestilence among you, and you will be given into the hand of the enemy.
When I break your supply of bread,{g} ten women will bake your bread in one oven and give back your bread by weight, and you will eat and not be satisfied.
“If in spite of this you do not listen to me, but walk contrary to me,
then I will walk contrary to you in fury, and I myself will discipline you seven times for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.
I will destroy your high places and cut down your incense altars{h} and throw your corpses on the corpses of your idols,{i} and my soul will reject you.
I will make your cities a ruin and lay your sanctuaries waste, and I will not smell your pleasing aromas.
I myself will lay waste the land, so that your enemies who settle in it will be appalled at it.
And you I will scatter among the nations, and I will unsheathe the sword after you. Your land will be a desolation, and your cities will be a ruin.
“Then the land will enjoy{j} its Sabbaths all the days that it lies desolate, while you are in your enemies’ land. Then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
All the days that it lies desolate it will have rest, the rest it did not have on your Sabbaths when you lived in it.{k}

As for those of you who are left, I will send faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a driven leaf will put them to flight. They will flee as one flees from the sword, and they will fall when no one is pursuing.
They will stumble over one another as if before the sword, though no one is pursuing. You will have no power to stand before your enemies.
You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will devour you.
And those of you who are left will rot away in your enemies’ lands because of their iniquity, and also because of the iniquities of their fathers they will rot away with them.
“But if they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers, in their unfaithfulness that they committed against me, and also that they walked contrary to me,
so that I walked contrary to them and brought them into the land of their enemies, if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they make amends for their iniquity,{l}
then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham I will remember,{m} and I will remember the land.

For the land will be abandoned by them and will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, while they make amends for their iniquity, because, and only because, they rejected my judgments and their soul abhorred my statutes.
Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or abhor them so as to destroy them utterly and break my covenant with them, for I am Yahweh their God.
But for their sake I will remember the covenant with their forefathers, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, to be their God. I am Yahweh.”
These are the statutes, the judgments, and the laws that Yahweh made between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.

notes.text: Hebrew ’elilim, “worthless things”; see the note at 19:4.
Hebrew ’even maskith, perhaps a stone carved with figures. The meaning is uncertain.

Part of the Greek text of this chapter (verses 2–16) survives in a Septuagint scroll from Qumran, 4QLXXLev-a, one of the oldest known manuscripts of the Greek Old Testament. Its readings at several points differ from the standard Septuagint text.
Hebrew mishkan, “tabernacle.” The Septuagint reads “my tabernacle,” and some ancient witnesses read “my covenant.”
Quoted in 2 Corinthians 6:16.
Hebrew qeri, found only in this chapter (verses 21–41), perhaps “in hostility” or “at random” (by chance, as if I did not matter).
Literally “break your staff of bread.”
Hebrew ḥammanim, perhaps incense altars or sun pillars. The Septuagint reads “wooden images made with hands.”
Hebrew gillulim, a contemptuous word for idols, perhaps “dung pellets.”
Or “pay off” or “make up for.” The Hebrew ratsah is the verb used for the acceptance of sacrifices; it recurs in verses 41 and 43.
Compare 2 Chronicles 36:21.
Or “they accept the punishment for their iniquity”; so in verse 43.

The patriarchs are listed in reverse order, Jacob, Isaac, Abraham. Their names are explained in Genesis: Abraham, “father of a multitude” (17:5); Isaac, “he laughs” (21:6); Jacob, “he grasps the heel” (25:26).

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, When a man makes a special vow{a} to Yahweh involving the value of persons,
the valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years old is to be about 20 ounces of silver,{b} by the sanctuary standard.{c}
If it is a female, the valuation is to be about 12 ounces.{d}
If the person is from five to twenty years old, the valuation of a male is to be about 8 ounces, and of a female about 4 ounces.{e}
If the person is from a month to five years old, the valuation of a male is to be about 2 ounces of silver, and for a female the valuation is to be about 1.2 ounces of silver.{f}
If the person is sixty years old or over, the valuation of a male is to be about 6 ounces, and of a female about 4 ounces.{g}
But if he is too poor to pay the valuation, he is to be presented before the priest, and the priest is to value him. The priest is to value him according to what the one who made the vow can afford.
“If it is an animal of the kind that may be presented as an offering to Yahweh, anything that he gives of such to Yahweh is to be holy.
He must not exchange it or substitute for it, good for bad or bad for good. If he does substitute one animal for another, then both it and its substitute will be holy.
If it is any unclean animal that may not be presented as an offering to Yahweh, he is to present the animal before the priest,
and the priest is to value it as either good or bad. As the priest values it, so it will be.
If he wishes to redeem it, he is to add a fifth to its valuation.
“When a man consecrates his house as holy to Yahweh, the priest is to value it as either good or bad. As the priest values it, so it will stand.
If the one who consecrated it wishes to redeem his house, he is to add a fifth to the price of its valuation, and it will be his.

“If a man consecrates to Yahweh part of a field of his own property, its valuation is to be in proportion to the seed needed for it: a field sown with about 6 bushels{h} of barley seed is to be valued at about 20 ounces of silver.
If he consecrates his field from the year of jubilee, it will stand at your full valuation.
But if he consecrates his field after the jubilee, the priest is to calculate the price according to the years that remain until the year of jubilee, and it is to be deducted from your valuation.
If the one who consecrated the field wishes to redeem it, he is to add a fifth to the price of its valuation, and it will remain his.
But if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it may no longer be redeemed.
When the field is released in the jubilee, it is to be holy to Yahweh, like a field that has been devoted.{i} It is to be the priest’s property.
If he consecrates to Yahweh a field that he has bought, which is not part of the field of his own property,
the priest is to calculate for him the amount of the valuation up to the year of jubilee, and he is to give the valuation on that day as a holy thing to Yahweh.
In the year of jubilee the field is to return to the one from whom it was bought, to whom the land belongs as his property.
Every valuation is to be by the sanctuary standard.{j}
“But a firstborn among animals, which as a firstborn belongs to Yahweh, no man may consecrate. Whether ox or sheep, it is Yahweh’s.
If it is among the unclean animals, he may ransom it according to your valuation, adding a fifth to it. If it is not redeemed, it is to be sold according to your valuation.
“But nothing that a man devotes to Yahweh of all that he has, whether person, animal, or field of his own property, may be sold or redeemed. Every devoted thing is most holy to Yahweh.
No person who has been devoted to destruction{k} from among people may be ransomed; he is surely to be put to death.
“Every tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the trees, belongs to Yahweh; it is holy to Yahweh.
If a man wishes to redeem any of his tithe, he is to add a fifth to it.
As for every tithe of the herd or flock, every tenth one that passes under the shepherd’s rod{l} is to be holy to Yahweh.
He must not inspect whether it is good or bad, nor make a substitute for it. If he does substitute for it, then both it and its substitute will be holy; it may not be redeemed.”
These are the commandments that Yahweh commanded Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.

notes.text: Or “an extraordinary vow”; see the note at 22:21. Persons vowed to Yahweh (compare 1 Samuel 1:11) were redeemed by paying their valuation to the sanctuary.

Hebrew “fifty shekels of silver.” The shekel was a unit of weight, about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams); fifty shekels were about 20 ounces (575 grams). The Septuagint reads “didrachms” throughout this chapter.
Literally “by the shekel of the sanctuary,” the official standard weight; see verse 25.
Hebrew “thirty shekels,” about 345 grams.
Hebrew “twenty shekels” (about 230 grams) and “ten shekels” (about 115 grams).
Hebrew “five shekels” (about 57.5 grams) and “three shekels” (about 34.5 grams).
Hebrew “fifteen shekels” (about 172.5 grams) and “ten shekels” (about 115 grams).
Hebrew “a homer,” a dry measure of about 6 bushels (about 220 liters), probably originally a donkey load (Hebrew ḥamor, “donkey”). The value is “fifty shekels of silver,” about 575 grams.
Hebrew ḥerem, something irrevocably given over to Yahweh, either to the sanctuary or to destruction; see verses 28–29.
Hebrew “the shekel of the sanctuary; twenty gerahs are to be the shekel.” The gerah was the smallest weight, 1/20 of a shekel, about 0.02 ounce (about 0.6 gram).
Or “who has been devoted” (Hebrew ḥerem). This refers to persons condemned under the ban, as in Deuteronomy 13:12–18 and Joshua 6:17, not to persons vowed in verses 2–8.
Literally “passes under the rod,” as a shepherd counts his flock (Jeremiah 33:13; Ezekiel 20:37).
